A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MMIE benchmark and scoring model. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, including v1's image-based rubric and case pages. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original LVLM benchmark scores, comparisons between automated and human scoring, field-level results, and qualitative error analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds scorer-bias comparisons, subset evaluations, an image-generation ablation, COCO evaluation, and scored case examples.

M1.justification: The MMIE construction and InternVL-2-4B scoring pipeline remain unchanged, including 800 annotated training responses and 200 evaluation examples. The original rubric graphics are retained. Additional annotation documentation, prompt reformulations, and supplemental applications do not establish a changed architecture, training objective, or core algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix A.8 adds evaluation on 100 COCO image-captioning examples, extending coverage beyond MMIE. The original four source datasets, three categories, and twelve fields remain unchanged. The 1,000-example MMIE subset changes sampling rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding main comparisons retain the four interleaved LVLMs, sixteen integrated combinations, and scoring baselines. New analyses reuse existing comparison methods. The Qwen2-VL-72b label corrects inconsistent naming in v1, whose experimental setup already specifies the 72b model.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands evaluation design: Appendix A.5 introduces a 1,000-example subset sampled across categories and fields; A.6 compares image-generating and text-only outputs on 100 matched inputs; A.8 evaluates 100 COCO examples using a caption-specific rubric. These are additional protocols, not demonstrated changes to the retained full-benchmark experiments.

E4.justification: Appendices A.4–A.8 add scorer comparisons stratified by category and model type, subset consistency checks, an image-generation ablation, and out-of-distribution generalization testing. Field analyses are expanded, and the eight retained illustrative cases gain scoring feedback. These substantially extend validation beyond v1's aggregate scorer comparison and existing error analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Additional cosine similarity, MSE, MAE, and Pearson results retain the existing reporting practice. Rerunning models on the new subset does not constitute repeated-trial uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Main Tables 3–5 retain their numerical results, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 6–11 and case scores. Table 9 reports MMIE-Score values of 53.46 without image generation versus 65.47 with it. Table 11 newly reports COCO cosine similarity of 0.673 for MMIE-Score versus 0.745 for GPT-4o. These are additional evaluations, not improvements to retained same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical contributions, proofs, or derivations. The added experiments and scoring instructions introduce no substantive mathematical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: a 20K interleaved benchmark, challenging LVLM performance, and a human-aligned automated scorer. The headline full-benchmark result of 65.47% for GPT-4o plus SDXL is unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning category bias, subset consistency, and the value of image outputs. Appendix A.8 explicitly limits applicability to open-ended multimodal generation and acknowledges potentially suboptimal transfer to other tasks. These qualify the retained reliability narrative, although A.4's claim of consistent superiority has exceptions in Table 6.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly documents field-based annotation sampling, twenty initial reference examples, and a graphical annotation interface. Appendix B describes content-filtering practices. The 800/200 training-evaluation counts were already disclosed in v1, and the new descriptions do not establish changed underlying curation. Code-access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including MMSearch, MME-CoT, MathVerse, and COCO, while removing some earlier evaluation references such as VHELM and Mementos. The related-work argument and positioning against existing interleaved benchmarks remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are largely retained. V2 adds ethics and reproducibility statements, organizes new appendix subsections and illustrative cases, and rewrites evaluation prompts. Editing also introduces visible textual errors, including 'Situational analysisme' in the prompts.

P2.justification: V2 adds six results tables and an annotation-interface figure. All eight existing case figures are reordered, reformatted, and expanded with feedback and scores. Core figures and rubric graphics are retained but relocated; Table 2 replaces checkmarks with Yes/No, and Table 5 removes metric-direction arrows.

improvement.justification: The added scorer analyses, COCO test, annotation documentation, and scored examples make the evaluation more transparent, while the tested 1K subset improves usability. Appendix A.8 also supplies useful applicability limits. These gains are qualified by weak reported human correlations, exceptions to A.4's claim of consistent superiority in Table 6, and newly corrupted prompt text. Overall, v2 provides useful additional scrutiny without decisively resolving the scorer-reliability concerns.
